concepts.name: Data Collection
concepts.description: Data is a collection of facts or information gathered through observation, surveys, or counting. Students learn to collect data from simple real-life situations such as classroom activities and daily observations.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to collect and record data from simple observations and surveys.

concepts.name: Organizing Data in Tables
concepts.description: Organizing data into tables makes it easier to read, compare, and analyze information. Tables provide a systematic way to present collected data.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to organize collected data into simple tables.

concepts.name: Frequency
concepts.description: Frequency represents the number of times a particular observation or category occurs in a dataset.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to determine and record the frequency of different observations.

concepts.name: Pictographs
concepts.description: Pictographs represent data using pictures or symbols, where each symbol stands for a fixed number of items. They provide an attractive and simple way to display information.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to read and interpret information presented in pictographs.

concepts.name: Bar Graphs
concepts.description: Bar graphs display data using bars of equal width and varying heights or lengths. They allow easy comparison between different categories.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to read and interpret simple bar graphs.

concepts.name: Comparing Data
concepts.description: Charts help compare quantities across different categories by observing the relative sizes of bars or symbols.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to compare values represented in charts and identify the highest and lowest quantities.

concepts.name: Creating Pictographs
concepts.description: Students create pictographs by selecting suitable symbols and assigning an appropriate value to each symbol.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to construct simple pictographs from given data.

concepts.name: Drawing Bar Graphs
concepts.description: Students represent numerical data using bar graphs with properly labeled axes and uniform scales.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to draw simple bar graphs from tabulated data.

concepts.name: Choosing Appropriate Representation
concepts.description: Different forms of charts are suitable for different types of data. Students learn to select an appropriate method for presenting information.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to choose a suitable chart to represent a given dataset.

concepts.name: Data-Based Decision Making
concepts.description: Charts help people make informed decisions by presenting information clearly and allowing easy comparison of data.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to use charts to answer questions and make simple decisions based on data.

concepts.name: Applications of Charts
concepts.description: Charts are used in schools, newspapers, weather reports, sports, business, and scientific studies to communicate information effectively.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify real-life situations where charts are used.

concepts.name: Interpreting Trends
concepts.description: Students observe patterns and trends in data to identify increases, decreases, and comparisons across categories.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to interpret simple trends shown in pictographs and bar graphs.

concepts.name: Understanding Smart Charts
concepts.description: This chapter develops students' ability to collect, organize, represent, interpret, and analyze data using tables, pictographs, and bar graphs.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to organize data, construct charts, interpret graphical information, and apply data-handling skills to solve everyday problems.
